definitions.name: Same-day sentiment
definitions.formula: S1(s,t) = sum(w*x) / sum(w) over articles assigned to stock s on trading day t
definitions.plain: The average tone of today's news about the stock.
definitions.why: The freshest signal available at the cutoff.
definitions.limits: Often based on a single headline, so it is noisy.
definitions.missing: Missing when no scored article is assigned to day t; rank becomes 0.5.

definitions.name: Five-day sentiment
definitions.formula: S5(s,t) = sum(w*x) / sum(w) over trading days t-4..t
definitions.plain: The average tone of the last five trading days of news.
definitions.limits: Slower to react; mixes old and new items equally.
definitions.missing: Missing when there is no scored article in the five days; rank becomes 0.5.

definitions.name: News-volume surprise
definitions.formula: NVS = ln(1 + N5) - ln(1 + 5*N_base/60), N5 = articles in t-4..t, N_base = articles in t-64..t-5
definitions.plain: Is the stock getting more coverage than usual, regardless of tone?
definitions.why: Separates 'more news' from 'better news' (arm C1 uses only this).
definitions.missing: Never missing after the 64-day warm-up (zero articles gives a defined value).

definitions.name: Abnormal sentiment
definitions.plain: Is recent tone better or worse than this stock's own usual tone?
definitions.limits: Needs history; unstable with few baseline articles.
definitions.missing: Missing if S5 is missing or fewer than 10 baseline articles; rank becomes 0.5.

definitions.name: Has recent news
definitions.plain: Whether there was any scored news in the last five trading days.
definitions.why: Lets the model treat 'no news' differently from 'neutral news'. Also defines sample S2.

definitions.name: Per-date ranks
definitions.formula: rank_frac = (average-tie rank - 0.5) / n among stocks with a value that date
definitions.plain: Each feature is compared across stocks on the same day, on a 0 to 1 scale.
definitions.why: Makes days comparable and limits outliers.
definitions.missing: Missing values get 0.5; if fewer than 5 stocks have a value that date, all get 0.5.

definitions.name: Execution-based label
definitions.formula: R_exec(t) = Open(t+11)/Open(t+1) - 1; Z_exec = R_exec / max(ATR%(t), 0.001); L_exec = 1 if Z_exec is in the top 30% that date
definitions.plain: The return you could actually have traded after seeing day t's news: enter at the next open, exit ten trading days later.
definitions.why: A signal formed at the cutoff cannot trade at that day's close.
definitions.limits: No equivalence with any close-to-close label is claimed.
definitions.missing: Missing if any needed bar is missing or non-positive, or fewer than 20 stocks that date.
